::: portfolio-section
## What are Quarto Listings?

A listing creates an organized collection of content from source documents or a metadata file. Instead of manually rebuilding a table of links, I can maintain the content information and let Quarto generate its display.

## Browse the work

Use the categories to choose a topic, the search box to filter entries, or the sorting controls to change their order. These entries link to existing pages in this portfolio.
:::

::: {#portfolio-work}
:::

::: portfolio-section
## How can listings support a professional portfolio?

Listings can organize dashboards, case studies, reports, design projects, and presentations. Categories help a recruiter find relevant work, while short descriptions explain what each item demonstrates.

For this portfolio, I use a separate YAML file to describe the homepage, CEP dashboard, and styling demonstration. These are learning artifacts on this site, not claims of additional completed client projects.

## How is this listing configured?

``` yaml
listing:
  id: portfolio-work
  contents: portfolio-items.yml
  type: table
  fields: [title, categories, description]
  sort: title
  categories: true
  filter-ui: true
  sort-ui: true
```

An entry in `portfolio-items.yml` looks like this:

``` yaml
- title: "CEP: AI-Assisted Meta-Analysis"
  path: dashboard.qmd
  categories: [Analytics, Research]
  description: "Project purpose, planned workflow, and evidence status."
```

The page uses a div with the matching ID to position the listing:

``` markdown
::: {#portfolio-work}
:::
```

## How will I add future work?

I can add another item with a title, path, category, and description, then render the website again. The file path should point to a real page. Quarto also supports grid and default listing layouts when a more visual presentation is useful.

## Reference

[Quarto: Document Listings](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-listings.html)
:::
